class.name: SteamAudioProbeBatch
class.brief_description: A box volume filled with sound probes, holding the baked data that pathing and baked reverb read at run time.
class.description: Probes are placed on the floors inside the volume, [member spacing] metres apart and [member height] above the surface, so the volume has to cover acoustic geometry to produce anything. Baking traces the whole scene and blocks while it runs. Bake once, save the result with [member data_path] and [member save_after_bake], and ship the file: on later runs the batch loads it instead of baking again. Baked data describes static geometry. Doors and other moving objects are handled at run time by [member SteamAudioPlayer.pathing_validation], so bake with them out of the way. One batch per level is the usual setup; sources use the first one that is registered.

method.name: bake
method.description: Generates probes inside the volume and bakes whatever is enabled, replacing any data the batch already holds. Blocks until it is done.

method.name: get_probe_count
method.description: How many probes the batch holds. Zero after a bake means the volume found no floors.

method.name: is_built
method.description: Whether the batch has probe data, whether baked or loaded.

method.name: load_data
method.description: Replaces the batch with data saved earlier by [method save_data].

method.name: save_data
method.description: Writes the baked probes and their data so a later run can load them instead of baking.

members.member: Threads to bake with. Zero uses half the processors.
Where the baked data lives. If the file exists it is loaded instead of baking; otherwise, with [member save_after_bake] on, the bake is written here.
How far above the floor probes are placed, roughly ear height.
Bake the shortest sound paths between every pair of probes, which is what [member SteamAudioPlayer.pathing] plays back.
Probes are treated as spheres of this radius when testing whether they can see each other.
Probe pairs further apart than this along the path have no path between them. Larger values let sound travel further, at the cost of bake time and memory.
Point samples per probe when testing visibility. The bake traces this squared rays per probe pair.
The fraction of rays that must get through for two probes to count as mutually visible.
Probes further apart than this are never considered mutually visible.
Load or bake as soon as the node enters the tree. Turn it off to control the timing yourself with [method bake] or [method load_data].
Ambisonic order of the baked impulse responses.
Bake reverb at every probe, which [member SteamAudioPlayer.baked_reverb] plays back instead of simulating reflections in real time.
How many times each ray reflects off geometry while baking.
Directions considered when generating diffusely reflected rays.
Length of the baked impulse responses, in seconds.
Sources closer than this to a surface are treated as being this far away, for energy purposes.
Rays traced from each probe while baking reverb.
Write the bake to [member data_path] when it finishes.
The box, in metres, centred on this node and turned by its rotation.
Distance between neighbouring probes. Halving it roughly quadruples both the probe count and the bake time.
